title: At last a Castilian squadron sinks a Tilimsānī one in the bay of Qādis
Victory before Ishbīliyya again: 2,300 Marīnids throw themselves at 17,000 Granadans and lose 1,750
The Marīnids rout a Castilian army at Cáceres in Extremadura, 1,500 Castilians lost for 80

Two years into the war: every Marīnid attempt on Granada has broken (four defeats at al-Mariyya, Sharīsh and twice before Ishbīliyya, 6,300 of their men lost to our 3,860), while the Marīnids range through Castile to El Escorial and Cáceres and rule the sea. The war costs 76 a month against an income of 60; sovereignty 99.7, Morocco's influence −13.4

A separate peace with the Marīnids. The court lets Fās understand that if Gharnāṭa throws its full weight into the war, Fās will lose it; if Gharnāṭa stands aside, Fās will win against Qashtāla. The Marīnids take the point: a white peace for Gharnāṭa, and their promise to respect its lands. Qashtāla is left to fight on alone

terms: Morocco promises to respect Granada's territory

source: Trent's account (about June 1362, after the save of 10 June; the exact day isn't given)
